title: A Name on the OR Roster
teaser: Roughly a month after accepting her offer, newly arrived general surgeon Maki Aizawa steps into Operating Room #2 as Ryuji Sakaguchi's first assistant on her very first morning.
gallery_caption: Maki Aizawa's first full day at Hoshimi Hospital—from morning orientation and her first elective hernia repair as first assistant to her post-op field notebook and evening walk past tomorrow's updated OR roster.

choices.choice_mk0_d1_a: "You passed today's case. Still, this was a routine elective repair—when we hit dense adhesions or fast-paced bellies, you'll have plenty more to drill."
choices.choice_mk0_d1_b: "Spotting a contralateral blind spot and speaking up on your very first day is a rock-solid start. The rest of your fluency will come naturally case by case."

nodes.mk0_001: At eight-thirty in the morning, the loudest few minutes of morning handover in the surgical doctors' office had just subsided, and sunlight slanted through the Venetian blinds onto the large magnetic OR schedule whiteboard on the wall.
nodes.mk0_002: When Ryuji Sakaguchi pushed open the door with his ward-round clipboard in hand, he immediately spotted a somewhat unfamiliar young figure standing in front of the schedule columns.
nodes.mk0_003: Her standard-issue Hoshimi Hospital white coat was pressed without a single crease, her light ash-brown hair tied neatly into two low tails over her shoulders as she tilted her head up, her gaze tracing cell by cell across this morning's roster for Operating Room #2.
nodes.mk0_004: Hearing footsteps behind her, she turned around at once. The instant she saw it was Ryuji Sakaguchi, her shoulders tensed slightly by reflex; she squared her onboarding folder against her chest and gave a proper, earnest bow:
nodes.mk0_005: "G-Good morning, Dr. Sakaguchi! I'm Maki Aizawa, officially reporting to the Department of Surgery today."
nodes.mk0_006: Sakaguchi paused, taking in her braced-for-battle posture, and couldn't help offering a warm smile:
nodes.mk0_007: "Morning, Dr. Aizawa. Didn't we already meet in the administrative conference room a month ago? Why are you greeting me like you're walking through the door for the very first time?"
nodes.mk0_008: Maki blinked, the tight corners of her mouth loosening a touch as she answered quietly, a little sheepish:
nodes.mk0_009: "Last time I came in a suit as an applicant visiting my seniors... Standing in the office in this white coat today is the first time it truly feels like I've become a colleague here. I'll really be counting on your guidance from here on out, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.mk0_010: "Did all the handover paperwork at your previous hospital wrap up smoothly?"
nodes.mk0_011: "Yes—all my closing inpatient charts and rotation sign-offs were completely handed over by the end of last week."
nodes.mk0_012: "Looks like HR moved nice and fast—the white coat fits you great!"
nodes.mk0_013: Accompanied by brisk footsteps, Asuka Shiromiya walked in from the hallway carrying a stack of sign-off forms. Maki immediately straightened up to greet her:
nodes.mk0_015: Asuka waved her hand with a bright smile, stepped between the two of them, and crisply finalized today's assignment:
nodes.mk0_016: "Welcome officially to Hoshimi Surgery, Dr. Aizawa. Just like we agreed at your interview, we won't schedule you as an independent primary surgeon at this stage—starting today, Dr. Sakaguchi will be your main preceptor for daily scrubbing-in and clinical mentoring; when it's time for milestone reviews down the road, Chief Surgeon Mido, Deputy Chief Pendragon, and Dr. Jinguji will evaluate you against our standards together."
nodes.mk0_017: As she spoke, Asuka raised a finger to tap the ten-o'clock slot already written neatly on the whiteboard—right beside primary surgeon "Ryuji Sakaguchi," in clean handwriting, stood "First Assistant: Maki Aizawa."
nodes.mk0_018: "There's a routine elective adult inguinal hernia repair in OR #2 at ten o'clock. Dr. Sakaguchi and I already talked it over—no need to stand off the table observing today. Go ahead and scrub right into first assistant."
nodes.mk0_019: Maki followed the director's finger back to that line on the whiteboard. Not a ward clerk trailing behind with charts, and not a second assistant tucked into the corner holding a retractor—behind her lenses, her eyes widened ever so slightly as tension and unmistakable anticipation rose across her face together.
nodes.mk0_020: "First assistant on my very first day...?! Yes, understood—I'll give it my full focus!"
nodes.mk0_021: "Don't put too much pressure on yourself—just rely on your everyday fundamentals. I have another morning meeting over in administration, so I'm officially leaving her in your hands, Dr. Sakaguchi!"
nodes.mk0_022: "Go ahead to your meeting, Director. We've got it covered."
nodes.mk0_023: Asuka turned briskly and left the office. Once her footsteps faded down the hall, Sakaguchi held out the chart clipboard for the ten-o'clock operation to Maki:
nodes.mk0_024: "Come on—we still have a little over an hour before ten. Let's head up to the surgical prep area and walk through our division of labor for today's case first."
nodes.mk0_025: Maki Aizawa (receiving the chart clipboard with both hands):
nodes.mk0_027: At nine twenty-five in the morning, the workstation outside the fourth-floor surgical suite was quiet and orderly.
nodes.mk0_028: Maki opened the female elective patient's admission record and preoperative lab sheets; in less than five minutes she had organized the key clinical details in her head and squared the corners of the lab slips neatly back under the clip.
nodes.mk0_029: "Elective open repair of a right indirect inguinal hernia. Coagulation profile and cardiopulmonary baseline are all within normal limits, the ward completed standard pre-op prep this morning, and anesthesia will be epidural with light sedation."
nodes.mk0_030: She looked up toward Sakaguchi beside her, her tone noticeably crisper and clearer than during their morning pleasantries:
nodes.mk0_031: "Dr. Sakaguchi, once we incise the external oblique aponeurosis and mobilize the hernia sac, do you prefer your first assistant to maintain steady medial retraction with a hook, or assist with blunt wet-sponge sweeping of the loose areolar tissue?"
nodes.mk0_032: Sakaguchi glanced at her with mild surprise:
nodes.mk0_033: "That's a sharp question. Looks like you paid plenty of attention to the primary surgeon's habits at the table back at your old hospital."
nodes.mk0_034: "When I stood at second assistant, I was further from the core field, so I could only watch closely whenever I had a spare moment holding a retractor for the first assistant... Honestly, it's been several months since I stood directly across from the primary surgeon managing exposure from start to finish."
nodes.mk0_035: At the mention of not having stood at first assistant for months, Maki's fingertips resting along the edge of the folder tightened almost imperceptibly.
nodes.mk0_036: Sakaguchi caught the small gesture. Rather than revisiting the old incident she had mentioned at her interview, he laid down the ground rules in a level, unmistakable voice:
nodes.mk0_037: "Aizawa, keep one thing straight in your head first—when we step into Room #2 in a bit, that operating table is not your second-round job interview."
nodes.mk0_038: Maki blinked slightly and looked up at him.
nodes.mk0_039: "I don't need you acting like a veteran who never hesitates on Day One. When dissecting planes, I prefer stabilizing the aponeurotic edge with a retractor first before sharp division; across from me, all you need to do is see the tissue plane clearly and stay in rhythm. If any anatomical course looks uncertain to you, or if something feels off under your fingers, speak up right away—never grit your teeth in silence out of fear of making a mistake."
nodes.mk0_040: Concrete, specific instructions worked better than any vague 'don't be nervous.' Maki's taut breathing visibly steadied as she gave an earnest nod:
nodes.mk0_041: "I'll remember that. Anything I'm unsure about, I won't keep bottled up—I'll report it to you right away."
nodes.mk0_042: Just then, Hiroko Sugimura paused as she wheeled a sterile instrument checklist cart past the prep station, offering them both a warm, welcoming smile:
nodes.mk0_043: "Morning, Dr. Sakaguchi. And you must be Dr. Maki Aizawa, who just reported in today? I'm Hiroko Sugimura, the scrub nurse assigned to Room #2 this morning—welcome to the operating suite."
nodes.mk0_044: Maki Aizawa (hurriedly giving a polite bow):
nodes.mk0_045: "Hello, Nurse Sugimura! I'm Maki Aizawa—thank you very much for working with me as first assistant today!"
nodes.mk0_046: "You're way too polite, Dr. Aizawa. I already set aside the size six-and-a-half sterile gloves HR listed for you right by the table, and the standard hernia tray and fine hemostats are all counted and ready—Dr. Sakaguchi speaks very directly at the table, though as long as everyone communicates clearly, he's not hard to work with at all."
nodes.mk0_047: "Undercutting me right to my face isn't very fair, Nurse Sugimura."
nodes.mk0_048: Hiroko gave a playful wink and wheeled her checklist cart into OR #2 ahead of them to set up the back table. That bit of easy collegial banter lightened the air in the corridor; Sakaguchi glanced up at the wall clock:
nodes.mk0_049: "Nine-forty—the patient's already being prepped for anesthesia. Go change into scrubs; I'll meet you at the scrub sinks in ten minutes."
nodes.mk0_051: There was none of a rookie's flustered fumbling. When Maki appeared before the sensor scrub sinks ten minutes later, she had changed into well-fitted short-sleeved OR scrubs, both ash-brown tails tucked meticulously without a stray strand inside a disposable blue surgical cap, a tie-on surgical mask contoured snugly beneath her nose bridge and glasses; from dispensing antiseptic soap to scrubbing fingertips, interdigital webs, and circumferentially past both elbows, every step of her surgical hand scrub was clean and textbook, showing real surgical rotation fundamentals.
nodes.mk0_052: The bright beam of the shadowless overhead lamp converged on the draped right lower quadrant inguinal field, while the steady, rhythmic pulse of the patient monitor echoed softly through quiet Operating Room #2.
nodes.mk0_053: Gowned and gloved in full sterile attire, Maki Aizawa stood at the first-assistant position directly across the narrow operating table from primary surgeon Ryuji Sakaguchi.
nodes.mk0_054: "Patient identity, right-sided surgical site mark, and epidural sensory level all verified. Sugimura—scalpel."
nodes.mk0_056: Incising skin and superficial Camper's and Scarpa's fascia to expose the glistening white external oblique aponeurosis—throughout the opening ten minutes of standard exposure, Maki's hands were remarkably disciplined. Whenever Sakaguchi touched a tiny subcutaneous bleeder with cautery or switched to scissors to open the aponeurosis, her dry-sponge dabbing and forceps counter-traction arrived half a beat ahead right where his hand wanted them—nowhere near an amateur who needed to be taught how to hold instruments.
nodes.mk0_057: Still, looking across the table, Sakaguchi could tell her shoulders remained slightly raised, checking his hand cues before every shift of her retractor as if unsure when she was allowed to speak up on her own.
nodes.mk0_058: Once the external oblique aponeurosis was divided along its fibers, the superficial anatomical plane of the inguinal canal opened cleanly into view.
nodes.mk0_059: "Aizawa, draw this inferomedial aponeurotic leaf a touch further down and laterally so the edge of the round ligament underneath comes into view."
nodes.mk0_061: Maki gripped the small right-angle retractor steadily with both hands and eased the incision margin two millimeters inferolaterally—yet the very next instant, her wrists paused almost imperceptibly in midair.
nodes.mk0_062: There was no bleeding, nor the slightest flicker in heart rate or blood pressure on the monitor, yet the smooth forward cadence at the table stalled for a distinct two seconds.
nodes.mk0_063: Sakaguchi stilled the Metzenbaum scissors in his right hand. Without scolding her or offering a vague 'pull harder,' he calmly raised his eyes to the young assistant across from him:
nodes.mk0_064: "Skip the 'I'm sorry' first. Tell me—why did your hand stop just now?"
nodes.mk0_065: Asked directly for her clinical reasoning, Maki's eyelashes fluttered lightly above her mask; her gaze dropped straight back to the tissue beneath the retractor tip as her voice returned at once to crisp, structured focus:
nodes.mk0_066: "As I drew the retractor inferolaterally just now, I felt a strand of loose tissue deep to the aponeurosis pull tighter than expected... I worried that applying full traction along that same vector might avulse or stretch a fine nerve branch adherent underneath, so I wanted to visualize it clearly before pulling further."
nodes.mk0_067: Sakaguchi glanced down along the tip of her retractor—and sure enough, a delicate nerve filament coursed obliquely across the superficial fascial plane.
nodes.mk0_068: "What your fingers felt was spot-on—that branch does need to be spared. Next time that happens, lift the tip of the retractor two millimeters more superficially and angle your pull parallel to the aponeurotic fibers so the deep plane doesn't take hard tension—try that angle now."
nodes.mk0_069: Maki eased her wrists two millimeters upward as instructed and swept gently outward along the plane. The taut areolar space opened effortlessly at once, leaving the fine nerve branch resting safely in the deep bed.
nodes.mk0_071: "It really released right away... Just shifting the tilt by two millimeters cleared it completely. The field is steady now, Dr. Sakaguchi!"
nodes.mk0_073: After that brief back-and-forth exchange, more than half of that anxious stiffness in Maki's shoulders melted visibly away.
nodes.mk0_074: The repair progressed smoothly into its middle phase—the body of the indirect hernia sac had been mobilized step by step, and they were advancing toward the medial margin of the deep inguinal ring to free the neck of the sac. Sakaguchi elevated the sac wall gently with atraumatic forceps in his left hand, his right hand positioning fine dissecting scissors along an inferomedial fascial fold to divide the last band of adherent fibers.
nodes.mk0_075: One second before the scissor blades closed, Maki—who had been watching the contralateral deep shadow with complete concentration—suddenly spoke up:
nodes.mk0_077: Her voice wasn't loud, yet there wasn't a trace of hesitant mumbling in it.
nodes.mk0_078: Sakaguchi froze the dissecting scissors immediately and looked up at her:
nodes.mk0_080: "Looking obliquely into the inferomedial rim of the deep ring from my first-assistant angle, there appears to be a very fine deep vascular communicating branch hugging the underside of that fascial reflection—it's slightly darker than the surrounding preperitoneal fat, and from the primary surgeon's straight-on view it's hidden right behind the fold. Cutting straight across here might nick the vessel wall."
nodes.mk0_081: The table went quiet for half a second. Keeping his left-hand traction steady, Sakaguchi leaned half a step to the side to peer behind the crease along the oblique angle Maki had indicated.
nodes.mk0_082: Where the surgical lamp slanted into that fascial crease barely three millimeters wide, a faint dark-blue venous contour truly clung to the underside of the fascia medial to the inferior epigastric vessels—not a catastrophic major vascular anomaly, yet nicking it blind would have stained the narrow deep-ring field with venous ooze and cost them ten extra minutes of meticulous hemostasis.
nodes.mk0_083: "Good eye—from straight on, that fold hid it completely. Sugimura, trade me a fine right-angle dissector and a peanut sponge."
nodes.mk0_084: Hiroko Sugimura (her eyes curving warmly above her mask as she passed the instruments cleanly):
nodes.mk0_085: "Here—dissector. You kept a wonderfully sharp eye on that contralateral blind spot, Dr. Aizawa."
nodes.mk0_086: Sakaguchi used the peanut sponge to sweep gently downward along the neck of the sac, teasing the fine communicating branch cleanly away into safe territory before looking up at Maki:
nodes.mk0_087: "I've got the neck of the sac elevated now. Use your retractor to gently shield that vascular fascial layer we just swept back while we finish the high ligation."
nodes.mk0_088: "Understood! Deep vessels are shielded and the field is completely clear—please go ahead."
nodes.mk0_089: With that concrete warning spoken and acted upon, the posterior floor reinforcement and layered closure over the second half of the procedure went forward without another awkward pause. Knowing just when to ease traction so the surgeon could approximate transversalis fascia, when to angle suture tails ready for scissors, and when to coordinate sponge and instrument counts with Hiroko before closure, Maki kept pace with steady, reliable poise.
nodes.mk0_090: "Lap pads, peanut sponges, needles, and instruments counted twice—all counts correct."
nodes.mk0_091: "Nice work, both of you. Final subcuticular stitch to finish—Aizawa, cut."
nodes.mk0_092: With one crisp snip, the suture tail was trimmed to just the right length. As a sterile dressing was smoothed neatly over the right lower quadrant incision, the elective repair wrapped up cleanly in under fifty minutes.
nodes.mk0_093: At eleven-fifteen, after confirming the patient's vitals were stable and handing her back to the surgical ward, Ryuji Sakaguchi signed off on the operative note and walked into the surgical staff lounge carrying a cup of warm water.
nodes.mk0_094: At the small round table by the window, Maki Aizawa—having changed back into her white coat only minutes ago—sat with her head lowered, a fine-nibbed fountain pen moving quietly and swiftly across her pocket-sized dark hardcover grid notebook.
nodes.mk0_095: Sakaguchi stepped over for a look—there were no copied textbook platitudes on the page, only clean cross-sectional line drawings of the inguinal hernia repair they had just finished: the direction of the reflected aponeurotic flap, the tiny communicating vessel tucked behind the deep-ring crease, and even the overly low tilt of her own retractor on that first pull, all marked out clearly with dashed lines and arrows.
nodes.mk0_096: Noticing his shadow beside the table, Maki stilled her pen, looked up, pushed her dark square-framed glasses up the bridge of her nose out of habit, and rose slightly sheepishly to her feet:
nodes.mk0_097: "Ah, Dr. Sakaguchi! Have you finished signing the operative record already? While the tactile feel from the table was still fresh in my hands, I wanted to sketch down those two exposure details first..."
nodes.mk0_098: "Stay seated and keep writing—you don't have to jump up every time I walk over. Honestly, when you told us at last month's interview that you sketch operative field diagrams within half an hour of scrubbing out, I figured at least part of that was interview polish—I didn't expect them to be this detailed."
nodes.mk0_099: Maki Aizawa (sitting back down, pressing her lips together lightly):
nodes.mk0_100: "It's because I'm not the quickest thinker on my feet... If I don't draw out the exact spot where my hands hesitated while it's still fresh, I'll easily repeat the same habit the next time I'm in that position."
nodes.mk0_101: Sakaguchi pulled out the chair across from her and sat down. Looking at those two earnest arrows on the grid paper, he set aside the light teasing and delivered his first formal teaching debrief as her preceptor:
nodes.mk0_102: "Since your notebook's already open, let me give you two pieces of teaching feedback while today's case is fresh."
nodes.mk0_103: Maki straightened her back at once, gripping her fountain pen as she looked earnestly at him:
nodes.mk0_105: "First, what you did well—while we were mobilizing the neck of the hernia sac, you spotted that fine vascular branch behind the fascial fold from the first assistant's oblique angle, and instead of hesitating because I'm your senior surgeon, you called out its exact position clearly before my scissors came down. That saved the patient unnecessary bleeding risk and saved me hemostasis time. Very solid first-assistant work."
nodes.mk0_106: At that specific praise, a quiet spark lit in Maki's eyes, though she didn't rush to celebrate—her gaze stayed focused, waiting for his second point.
nodes.mk0_107: "Second, a habit you need to break—ten minutes in, when retracting the external oblique aponeurosis, you sensed tension over the deep nerve filament. Stopping your hand was the right call; pausing silently in place for two seconds until I stopped my scissors and asked why was not."
nodes.mk0_108: Sakaguchi tapped beside the first dashed arrow on her notebook page, his voice calm yet unmistakable:
nodes.mk0_109: "Losing two seconds in a routine elective case doesn't hurt anyone, but down the road in a brisk, bleeding laparotomy, a silent freeze from the first assistant forces the primary surgeon to split focus guessing whether your grip slipped or you lost the plane. Next time something feels tight under your fingers, report 'deep tension' out loud the exact instant your hand stops—turn your judgment straight into shared team information. Clear?"
nodes.mk0_110: Maki bent her head, quickly jotted "Call out tension aloud the instant hand stops" beside the dashed arrow, and gave a firm nod:
nodes.mk0_111: "Understood! I used to worry that speaking up abruptly might break the primary surgeon's train of thought—I didn't realize freezing without a word disrupts the rhythm even more... I'll make sure to fix that on my very next case."
nodes.mk0_112: Finishing the note, she rested the tip of her pen, raised her eyes toward Sakaguchi across the table, and asked softly with candid trepidation:
nodes.mk0_113: "Um, Dr. Sakaguchi... For my very first day working at Hoshimi, did my performance at the table today reach your passing mark for a first assistant?"
nodes.mk0_114: Looking into her earnest eyes, Sakaguchi didn't humor her with polite flattery, answering matter-of-factly instead:
nodes.mk0_115: "For today's routine repair, you passed. Still, this is about as clean as anatomical planes get in an elective minor procedure—once you scrub into deep abdominal cases or heavy adhesions, the demands on sustained traction stamina and split-second adaptation go way up. You still have plenty of hard homework ahead before you can stand on your own."
nodes.mk0_116: Hearing an unvarnished, demanding standard didn't discourage Maki in the slightest—instead, the brow she had kept furrowed all morning relaxed completely, and she answered in a noticeably clearer, brighter voice:
nodes.mk0_117: "Yes! What I feared most was that you'd only say nice things to go easy on a newcomer—knowing I'm standing on the passing line right now, and knowing exactly what to build next, puts my mind completely at ease!"
nodes.mk0_118: Seeing the faint tension still lingering even in her fingertips, Sakaguchi offered a warm smile:
nodes.mk0_119: "Stepping up to the table with a brand-new partner on Day One and spotting a contralateral blind spot in time to warn the primary surgeon off a vessel is already a rock-solid start. You cleared the passing mark easily—the rest of your coordination fluency will smooth out naturally as we log cases one by one."
nodes.mk0_120: Maki blinked for half a second before the breath she had been holding in her chest finally settled; behind her glasses, her eyes curved into a genuine, uncluttered smile:
nodes.mk0_121: "Thank goodness... Right up until we walked through the OR doors after scrubbing, I kept worrying I might cause trouble for you and Nurse Sugimura on my first day."
nodes.mk0_122: Sakaguchi took a sip of warm water, stood up, and picked up his chart folder from the table:
nodes.mk0_123: "Nobody masters surgery in a day—independent primary-surgeon privileges will come step by step as you clear formal evaluations. Until then, whenever my team's on the board, the first-assistant spot across from me is always open to you. Come on—let's grab lunch in the cafeteria first, and this afternoon I'll take you up to the ward to check on how our hernia patient is recovering."
nodes.mk0_124: Maki carefully closed the grid notebook filled with fresh annotations, slipped it into her white-coat pocket, and rose briskly to follow him:
nodes.mk0_125: "Right! Thank you for taking me along on afternoon rounds too!"
nodes.mk0_126: By five-fifty in the evening, afternoon postoperative rounds and her first-day admission paperwork had all wrapped up smoothly. After confirming that this morning's hernia repair patient had a dry dressing and could turn over and chat comfortably in bed, Maki's first workday had finally reached quitting time.
nodes.mk0_127: Late-day sunlight slanted through the tall window at the end of the surgical corridor, washing the quiet floor in warm amber.
nodes.mk0_128: Changed back into neat commuter clothes with her bag slung over one shoulder, Maki walked side by side with Sakaguchi toward the exit. After a few unhurried steps in the looser after-hours quiet, she hesitated briefly before glancing over and speaking softly:
nodes.mk0_129: "Um, Dr. Sakaguchi... There's actually one small thing I felt too awkward to bring up during last month's interview."
nodes.mk0_131: "Director Shiromiya, Dr. Kaori Miyama in Emergency, and I... actually graduated from the same women's medical university. I was two classes behind them."
nodes.mk0_132: Sakaguchi slowed half a beat, recalling that the same university name had indeed flashed across the education line of her CV on interview day, and chuckled:
nodes.mk0_133: "And here I thought it was some big secret. No wonder your resume looked familiar—if you're their junior from the same school, how come you didn't breathe a word of it at the interview?"
nodes.mk0_134: Maki Aizawa (shaking her head lightly, her expression earnest and candid):
nodes.mk0_135: "We didn't actually know each other personally back in school—Director Shiromiya and Dr. Miyama were already standout figures two years ahead of me. Besides, I was applying to be a surgeon; bringing up 'I'm the director's alumna junior' across an interview table—whether I got rejected or hired—would have felt like hoping my seniors would cut me slack out of school ties."
nodes.mk0_136: She adjusted the strap on her shoulder, gazing out the corridor window toward the quiet hospital courtyard, a note of genuine reflection entering her voice:
nodes.mk0_137: "Still, over the past couple of years, Director Shiromiya and Hoshimi Hospital really have come up constantly among graduates and younger students back at our alma mater."
nodes.mk0_138: "What do people back at your school say about this place?"
nodes.mk0_139: "All kinds of things. Plenty of women in my class who spend all day buried in paperwork at big general hospitals without getting OR table time are genuinely envious—they admire Director Shiromiya for breaking rigid seniority customs and actually giving young women surgeons assistant slots and real mentoring."
nodes.mk0_140: She paused, sugarcoating nothing as she shared the other half of the talk:
nodes.mk0_141: "Of course, there's plenty of private skepticism too... Some people say Director Shiromiya only took over the hospital from her mother at twenty-three and might just be playing around on family legacy; others wonder whether clinical standards under such a young leadership team must be lax—too loose to teach real surgical craft."
nodes.mk0_142: Listening to that candid outside chatter, Sakaguchi gave a quiet smile; instead of launching into a speech defending Asuka, he simply tossed the question back:
nodes.mk0_143: "And now that Dr. Aizawa has walked through the door and worked a full day here herself—what's your verdict?"
nodes.mk0_144: Maki turned to meet his eyes, her gaze behind her lenses clear and bright:
nodes.mk0_145: "Checking protocols at the prep station this morning, standing a full fifty minutes as first assistant in Room #2, and the silent-pause habit you called me on afterward... Not one part of today could be bluffed through by playing around or lowering standards. I can't control what rumors say outside, but I'm really glad I worked up the courage to send in my resume last month."
nodes.mk0_146: As they spoke, the two of them passed the surgical office doorway—and through the half-open door, they happened to catch sight of the magnetic schedule whiteboard Maki had stood gazing up at alone that morning.
nodes.mk0_147: Tomorrow's operative schedule had already been updated.
nodes.mk0_148: In the slot for tomorrow morning's first elective general surgery case—
nodes.mk0_149:
Primary Surgeon: Ryuji Sakaguchi.
First Assistant: Maki Aizawa.
nodes.mk0_150: Her name was still written there, crisp and unmistakable.
nodes.mk0_151: Maki stopped in her tracks and looked quietly up at that line for two full seconds.
nodes.mk0_152: The shadow of retreating into a second-assistant corner months ago at her old hospital out of fear of clinical consequences hadn't vanished by magic in a single day; walking into the scrub room tomorrow morning, her pulse would probably still run a few beats faster than her seniors'. Yet as she looked at her own name on the OR roster, her fingers no longer clenched the hem of her coat the way they had at dawn.
nodes.mk0_153: Turning to face Sakaguchi beside her, she gave a poised, unhurried bow and offered her most natural smile of the entire day:
nodes.mk0_154: "Thank you so much for guiding me through the table on my first day, Dr. Sakaguchi. I'll review all the chart materials ahead of time for tomorrow morning's case too—I look forward to working with you!"
nodes.mk0_155: Sakaguchi nodded back, his tone steady and warm:
nodes.mk0_156: "Today was just Case One. We have plenty more operations waiting for us ahead. Welcome to Hoshimi, Dr. Aizawa."
nodes.mk0_158: Watching the young surgeon walk briskly and squarely toward the elevator lobby ahead, Ryuji Sakaguchi glanced once more through the half-open doorway at the newly added name on the OR whiteboard, then turned toward the cool dusk beyond the hospital gates.
